order.why_here: Builds the structure itself: nested dicts, end markers, and the walk that every later problem reuses.
First use of the walk as a tool: one path tests a word against every root at once, and stopping early gives the shortest.
The walk becomes a DFS: a wildcard forces branching, and the trie prunes every branch that cannot match.
The DFS moves onto a grid, with the trie as a guide that prunes paths and shrinks as words are found.
Nodes now carry payloads (word lists) so a prefix query returns candidates directly inside a backtracking search.
Rewrites a two-sided query into one prefix by inserting suffix#word keys, with the best index stored at every node.
Suffix matching becomes prefix matching on a reversed trie walked backwards over a bounded buffer.
Closes the chapter: a live cursor in the trie plus per-node frequency maps that turn every keystroke into a ranked answer.
